fi-horabagrus-brachysoma.title: Sun Catfish
fi-horabagrus-brachysoma.summary: The sun catfish, Horabagrus brachysoma, is a large bagrid catfish endemic to the state of Kerala in south-western India. Also sold as the bullseye, solar, eclipse or golden red-tailed catfish, it is…
rows: Feeds on smaller fish, invertebrates and plant matter in nature, although thankfully there is no need to offer live ' feeder' fish in the aquarium.
Endemic to the state of Kerala in south-western India .
notes: It's a nocturnal species, so provide dim lighting and refuges in the form of big chunks of bogwood , tangles of beech branches, large rocks or lengths of plastic piping of a suitable bore.
Ensure that any decor is either secured or is too heavy to be moved around by the fish.

fi-kryptopterus-bicirrhis.title: Glass Catfish
fi-kryptopterus-bicirrhis.summary: The glass catfish, Kryptopterus vitreolus, is a transparent silurid catfish from coastal river basins of peninsular and southeastern Thailand. Available in the trade for decades, it was widely…
rows: schools meaning a group of 6 or more specimens is the minimum recommended.
Carnivore / micropredator. Probably a predator feeding on small invertebrates and zooplankton in nature.
Known only from a series of coastal river basins of Peninsular Thailand draining into the Gulf of Thailand south of the Isthmus of Kra , plus a handful of rivers draining the…
notes: Best kept in a well-decorated set-up with some surface or floating vegetation since it appears to prefer relatively dim conditions.

The addition of dried leaf litter and/or alder cones would further emphasise the natural feel while the tannins and other chemicals released by these as they decompose are considered beneficial for fishes from blackwater environments.
Most “glass catfish” in the trade are Kryptopterus vitreolus; K. bicirrhis is rarer. Care is similar.
